emergencies.title: Spacesuit Pressure Leak (EVA)
emergencies.summary: A spacesuit pressure leak during an EVA may threaten astronaut safety and require immediate termination of the spacewalk and return to the spacecraft.
steps: Use the spacesuit's available contingency life-support capability, as applicable.
If the astronaut cannot return independently, initiate the applicable crew-rescue procedure.
Follow the mission-specific airlock recovery procedure.
emergencies.sourceNote: Based on NASA Exploration EVA System Concept of Operations, Revision B, Section 9.1.1. Simplified summary; not an approved operational checklist.

emergencies.title: Suspected Cardiac Arrest
emergencies.summary: A suspected cardiac arrest requires immediate notification of the Crew Medical Officer and intervention by trained responders using approved onboard medical procedures.
steps: Assess the astronaut's responsiveness and breathing.
Notify other crew members and mission medical support.
If cardiac arrest is identified, trained responders follow the approved onboard CPR and resuscitation protocol.
Use appropriate onboard medical equipment under the applicable protocol.
Record the emergency and medical interventions.
emergencies.sourceNote: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1, Revision C establishes medical training requirements. This response sequence is proposed for AstraCare and is not a NASA-certified cardiac-arrest checklist.

emergencies.title: Spacecraft Depressurization
emergencies.summary: Loss of spacecraft cabin pressure requires prompt crew notification and implementation of the applicable spacecraft emergency procedure.
steps: Recognize and report the depressurization emergency.
Follow the spacecraft's approved emergency procedure.
Isolate the affected module when directed by the procedure.
Prepare for emergency evacuation if required.
emergencies.sourceNote: High-level summary based on NASA ISS emergency-response training information; not an exact NASA flight checklist.
